title: Why You Never Forget How To Ride A Bike
hook: You learned to cycle aged five, but have not ridden in decades. You still can.

narration.text: You can remember how to ride a bicycle for your entire life.
This is thanks to something called procedural memory.
It is a type of long-term memory for skills and habits.
These memories are stored in different brain areas than factual memories.
Once learned, these motor skills become deeply ingrained and automatic.
This makes them much harder to forget, even with long breaks.
It is why you can still tie your shoelaces without thinking.
This amazing ability keeps many everyday activities effortless.
What other skills have you remembered after a long time?

description: Ever wondered why you can hop on a bike after years and still ride it perfectly? It is all thanks to procedural memory. This video explains how your brain stores skills and habits, making them incredibly resistant to forgetting.
topic: Why you can remember how to ride a bike years after last doing it, explaining procedural memory consolidation.
